reviews.title: If you are a chemistry teacher thinking about using this app, think again.
reviews.text: I have to use Pearson’s Chemistry: A Molecule Approach, 6e for my chemistry and AP chemistry class in school. This book has been nothing but a pain for me to use. Many of the answers in the book are blatantly incorrect and make no sense and to get the practice problem answers you have to scroll all the way to the chapter you are on in the answer key. The app has an option to bookmark the page you are on which I thought would be very helpful until I realized that this god forsaken app recognizes the multi page long answer key as a singular page meaning that when you book mark it it just returns to the very start of the answer key. The way it explains chemistry is so confusing and makes no sense even when it is just explaining a very simple concept. The entire book feels like it was made lizard people or AI. I have no idea if other books on this app are similar however clearly there was no thought put into these books and considering how expensive they are to rent or buy I would highly not recommend.

reviews.title: Over integration of AI and new vocab features
reviews.text:
I have been using Pearson+ for quite some time, and one of my favorite features was the ability to tap a highlighted vocabulary word and instantly see its definition in a simple white popup. It was fast, unobtrusive, and allowed me to continue reading without losing my place or breaking my concentration.

Unfortunately, that feature has now been replaced with the AI Study Tool panel. Instead of a quick glossary definition, every vocabulary lookup now opens the AI sidebar. While AI can be helpful in some situations, it is unnecessary for something as simple as defining a vocabulary term. This change interrupts the reading experience, takes up more screen space, and makes studying less efficient.

It feels like Pearson is trying to incorporate AI into every aspect of the textbook, even when it makes the user experience worse. Not every feature needs AI, and not every student wants AI involved in their learning. Sometimes a simple, well-designed tool is the better solution.

The biggest issue is the lack of user choice. Students learn in different ways, and we should be able to customize our learning experience. If someone prefers the AI Study Tool, that’s great. But those of us who preferred the original glossary popup should have the option to use it instead. Giving users the ability to choose between the classic glossary popup and the AI panel would make the app far more flexible and student-friendly.

Technology should enhance learning, not force every interaction through AI

reviews.title: Major accessibility and usability issues on iOS
reviews.text:
Pros of this app:
- search function
- study videos and additional materials
- ability to change font sizes

Cons:
- dark mode hides CRUCIAL information (like formulas) which is a major accessibility issue
- no way to take margin notes
- highlighting doesn’t work on symbols (and symbols are hugely important in science textbooks)
- no way to bookmark images
- “feedback” option is a black hole and the native iOS browser is not supported so contacting support from within the app is impossible
- highlighting constantly flips the page instead of selecting text

This is such a frustrating app to use and it’s really disappointing considering eTextbooks are basically a requirement in order to keep up with education these days.

reviews.title: Seriously bad UX
reviews.text:
1) I’m really sick of the textbook “page” snapping back to the to the top when I accidentally click forward to the next page but then try to immediately go back. (Moving to the next page is way too easy to do by mistake with just a tap when trying to summon the menu for contents, etc.)

2) MAKE IT EASIER TO OPEN THE BOOK. When I tap on the textbook, I expect to start reading within seconds. But no: I’m brought to a second screen that puts tutorial videos at the top, then has a much smaller “read textbook” button that I have to scroll down to.

3) The “audiobook” feature is just a bad AI reader that makes it more difficult to understand than reading the text.

4) Solutions at the back of the book have their numbers cut off so instead of Problem 43 I just see the number “3.”

5) Diagrams seem to be in a png format, so in dark mode it’s impossible to read them since it’s blue, red, and black pictures/text on a black background.

6) There’s no way to report content errors or other things that need to be corrected/adjusted

7) My view history should have WAY more than just the last three pages I viewed. I frequently need to reference at least three pages to answer a problem, but when I do that, the end-of-chapter exercises are no longer listed for me to easily jump back to. (And when I do jump back, it goes to the top of the page instead of where I left off.)

Be careful when using this, can’t trust it’s telling you whether your answer is actually right or wrong unless you make sure to look over why you got it wrong. You may find you were actually right.

reviews.title: Formatting & Subscription Hostage
reviews.text: My text, Marieb A&P 12, is so poorly formatted that I cannot highlight numbers, special characters such as the percentage sign or the latin alphabet, and occasionally even just words that happen to be bolded, italicized, or links. There is no way to use a stylus to write notes directly on the pages. A PDF in a browser would be more functional. Also, ALL, and I do mean every single, study aide that comes with my book is missing from the app. I MUST use a browser to access these materials. However, their subscription study program and AI generated materials that are both inaccurate and not customizable (meaning every little detail I don’t need to know is included against my will) are very available. It is ridiculous that I am paying over $100 to temporarily access this text and I can’t even mark it up, use the built in study materials without using another app, or even use the study materials that are available because they’re unhelpful and outside of my budget. This is highway robbery and I don’t have any coins to spare. Do better.

reviews.title: App won’t open/load the textbook
reviews.text:
This app needs to do one thing well: open my text book. Why? Because I need to read the textbook. Can this app do that? No, it can’t open the dang textbook. Why? I don’t know, if I’d found that out, I wouldn’t be forced to leave this review. This app can’t do the one thing it needs to do. Seriously… this app is worthless to me.

Also, it’s just a way for this company to market ads for subscription fees. Yes, it will collect your data too and likely sell it. I prefer the other textbook apps that actually work and also that don’t berate me with adds.

Guess what? In the time it’s taken me to write this review, my textbook still hasn’t loaded or opened even though it’s been downloaded. The app is probably too busy collecting my data to even work right.

reviews.title: Horrible
reviews.text: I was able to get through one of my classes up until November without needing the textbook, but eventually needed it for a complex topic. I signed up for the subscription to gain access to the textbook, and was very unsatisfied with the performance of the app. The app constantly glitches and signs me out of my devices, and I wasn’t able to use it for two weeks until I figured it out. Not only that, but now that the semester is over, I am still paying the monthly subscription without needing the textbook. I’ve tried cancelling it through the website and app, but there is no way to cancel the etextbook access. If this is advertised as a subscription, you should be able to cancel it at any time. I called customer service, and was told I was in a 6 month plan and my last charge would be on April 4, 2026. The app is finicky, and the subscriptions are totally shady. Please be cautious before making a purchase on Pearson Plus, you are locked into a literal contract for a textbook.
